def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract:
## Definition

Let $\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]) with a declared sampling or assignment mechanism. A **sampling unit** is one indexed unit that the declared mechanism treats as an indivisible draw or assignment object. Its **unit record** contains the complete observed data attached to that unit, including repeated measurements or labels that the analysis keeps together. Examples of sampling units are individuals, matched pairs, clusters, time blocks, and treatment-assignment units.

The declared mechanism also specifies a measurable unit-record space $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$ and represents each unit record as an element of $\mathcal Z$. The record space may be the whole data space or one record-valued component of it; the convention is part of the experiment's sampling or assignment contract.

A **resampling unit** is the complete unit record or predeclared group of records that one draw of a resampling procedure selects. A procedure is **unit-compatible for a stated target** when it declares which records are sampled together and does not split a bundle whose joint sampling or assignment dependence is part of that target's data-generating design. Unit compatibility describes the procedure's input and dependence contract; it does not itself establish exact or asymptotic validity. A validity claim requires a separate theorem with hypotheses matched to the sampling or assignment law, target, and resample-size regime.

The conditional bootstrap law of observed units is a law on resampled data records given the fixed observations. When defined, a Bayesian posterior is instead a conditional law on parameter values under a specified prior and joint parameter-data model. They have different state spaces and are not identified by this definition. In particular, neither law determines the other.
def-empirical-measure:
## Definition

Let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$ be a measurable unit space ([[def-measurable-space]]), let $n\ge1$, and fix an observed ordered tuple $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathcal Z$. Its **empirical measure** is the set function
$$P_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{z_i},\qquad P_n(A)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n1\{z_i\in A\}\quad(A\in\mathcal F),$$
where $\delta_{z_i}$ is the Dirac set function from [[def-dirac-measure]]. Repeated observations contribute once for each index at which they occur. The statement that $P_n$ is a probability measure is established in [[lem-empirical-measure-is-a-probability-measure]].
lem-uniform-law-on-finite-subset-familie:
## Statement

For $n\ge0$, let $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with $[0]=\varnothing$. For an integer $r$ with $0\le r\le n$, let
$$\mathcal S_{n,r}:=\{I\subseteq[n]:|I|=r\}.$$
Then $\mathcal S_{n,r}$ is finite and nonempty, and assigning weight $1/|\mathcal S_{n,r}|$ to each member defines a finite probability space on $\mathcal S_{n,r}$.
lem-empirical-measure-is-a-probability-m:
## Statement

For every $n\ge1$, every measurable space $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$, and every observed tuple $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathcal Z$, the empirical measure $P_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{z_i}$ from [[def-empirical-measure]] is a probability measure on $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$.
alg-delete-d-jackknife-replicates:
## Definition

**Input.** Let $n\ge2$, let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$ be the declared measurable space of unit records, and fix observed records $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathcal Z$ whose resampling unit satisfies [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]]. For each tuple length $m$, declare a sample sigma-algebra $\mathcal F_m$ on the ordered tuple space $\mathcal Z^m$. Choose $1\le d<n$ and provide a statistic $T_{n-d}:(\mathcal Z^{n-d},\mathcal F_{n-d})\to(\mathbb R^q,\mathcal B_q)$, where $q\ge1$ is finite and $\mathcal B_q$ is the declared target sigma-algebra; "statistic" has the measurable-map meaning in [[def-statistic-and-estimator]].

Write $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for the indexing set; the finite subset law on these indices is established in [[lem-uniform-law-on-finite-subset-families]].

**Procedure.** Form $\mathcal I_{n,d}:=\{I\subseteq[n]:|I|=d\}$. For every $I\in\mathcal I_{n,d}$, list the indices in $[n]\setminus I$ in increasing order and compute
$$\widehat\theta_{(-I)}:=T_{n-d}((z_i)_{i\in[n]\setminus I}).$$
Let $M_{n,d}:=|\mathcal I_{n,d}|$ and return the full collection of replicates together with the uniform average
$$\overline\theta_{(-d)}:=\frac1{M_{n,d}}\sum_{I\in\mathcal I_{n,d}}\widehat\theta_{(-I)}.$$
The finite, nonempty subset family and its uniform law are justified by [[lem-uniform-law-on-finite-subset-families]].

This algorithm defines the replicates and their average only. Any variance or bias scaling is a separate statistic with an explicitly stated target; no scaling is implicit in the term **delete-d jackknife**, and the algorithm asserts no validity theorem.
alg-uniform-subsampling-without-replacem:
## Definition

**Input.** Let $n\ge2$, let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$ be the declared measurable space of unit records, and fix observed records $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\mathcal Z$ whose resampling unit satisfies [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]]. Declare a sample sigma-algebra $\mathcal F_b$ on the ordered tuple space $\mathcal Z^b$, choose $1\le b<n$, and provide a statistic $T_b:(\mathcal Z^b,\mathcal F_b)\to(\mathbb R^q,\mathcal B_q)$, where $q\ge1$ is finite and $\mathcal B_q$ is the declared target sigma-algebra; "statistic" has the measurable-map meaning in [[def-statistic-and-estimator]].

Write $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for the indexing set; the finite subset law on these indices is established in [[lem-uniform-law-on-finite-subset-families]].

**Procedure.** Draw $I$ uniformly from the finite family $\mathcal I_{n,b}:=\{J\subseteq[n]:|J|=b\}$, without replacement; list its indices in increasing order; and return the subsample $(z_i)_{i\in I}$ and statistic value $T_b((z_i)_{i\in I})$. The uniform law is well-defined by [[lem-uniform-law-on-finite-subset-families]].

This is subsampling without replacement. It is different from drawing $b$ indices independently with replacement. The procedure defines a finite law only; validity requires a separate theorem for the data-generating design and asymptotic regime.
alg-n-out-of-n-bootstrap-from-empirical-:
## Definition

**Input.** Let $n\ge1$, let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$ be the declared measurable space of sampling units, and fix the observed ordered tuple $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Let $P_n$ be its empirical probability measure from [[def-empirical-measure]] and [[lem-empirical-measure-is-a-probability-measure]]. Declare a sample sigma-algebra $\mathcal F_n$ on the ordered tuple space $\mathcal Z^n$ and provide a statistic $T_n:(\mathcal Z^n,\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathbb R^q,\mathcal B_q)$, where $q\ge1$ is finite and $\mathcal B_q$ is the declared target sigma-algebra; "statistic" has the measurable-map meaning in [[def-statistic-and-estimator]].

Write $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for the indexing set.

**Procedure.** Draw indices $I_1,\ldots,I_n$ independently and uniformly from $[n]$, so repeated indices are allowed. Set $Z_j^*:=z_{I_j}$ for $j=1,\ldots,n$. Return the bootstrap tuple $(Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_n^*)$ and the replicate $T_n(Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_n^*)$. Generate further replicates by repeating the index draws with fresh randomness. These are resampling units only when the tuple entries satisfy the unit contract in [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]].

The conditional IID law of the draws is proved in [[thm-bootstrap-draws-are-conditionally-iid-empirical-law]]. This algorithm does not claim that its conditional law consistently approximates any sampling law; such validity requires separate hypotheses and a separate theorem.
thm-bootstrap-draws-are-conditionally-ii:
## Statement

Fix $n\ge1$, write $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $(\mathcal Z,\mathcal F)$ be a measurable unit space, and fix an observed tuple $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Let $P_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{z_i}$ be its empirical probability measure. For the bootstrap algorithm [[alg-n-out-of-n-bootstrap-from-empirical-law]], equip the conditional index vector $(I_1,\ldots,I_n)$ with the finite uniform law on $\Omega_n:=\{f:[n]\to[n]\}$ and set $Z_j^*=z_{I_j}$. For every $A_1,\ldots,A_n\in\mathcal F$,
$$\mathbb P^*(Z_1^*\in A_1,\ldots,Z_n^*\in A_n)=\prod_{j=1}^nP_n(A_j).$$
Thus, conditional on the fixed observed tuple, $Z_1^*,\ldots,Z_n^*$ are independent random elements with common law $P_n$ ([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]).
